name: the Ochrel
identity: Mesa-dwelling potters, glassblowers and star-readers who run the great caravans across the red country.
architecture: Cool adobe towns carved into mesa walls, wind-towers that pull the breeze indoors, kilns glowing at dusk, and shady courtyards around deep wells.

festivals.name: the Night of Open Kilns
festivals.description: Every kiln in town is opened at once, and families trade their best pots by firelight.

festivals.name: the Long Shade
festivals.description: Everyone naps through the hottest day of the year and then celebrates all night under the stars.

festivals.name: the Star Reckoning
festivals.description: The star-readers announce the new calendar from the highest roof, and get it very slightly wrong on purpose so there is something to argue about.

pride: Their caravans, which kept the Long Roads alive through the Hush, and glass so clear you forget it is there.

makersMarks: a thumbprint pressed into the clay before firing
a small star etched into the glass
a knot pattern unique to the maker's caravan

relations.note: Partners in the glass and spice trade, rivals over who invented the lighthouse lens.
Glass and dyes up the mountain; tea and slate down to the mesas.
Both read the stars to cross empty country, and their star-readers write to each other.
